entities.name: Siege of Alexandria
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Siege of Alexandria, also known as the Alexandrian War, was a pivotal battle fought in 48-47 BC between the forces of Julius Caesar and the Egyptian pharaoh Ptolemy XIII. This momentous clash took place in the ancient city of Alexandria, which was then a major center of learning and culture.

The siege was a complex web of alliances and rivalries between the Roman Republic, the Ptolemaic Kingdom, and the Seleucid Empire. At its core, it was a struggle for control of the Mediterranean world and the resources of Egypt. The Roman legions, led by Caesar, ultimately emerged victorious, paving the way for the Roman conquest of Egypt and the eventual rise of the Roman Empire.

The consequences of the siege were far-reaching. It marked the end of the Ptolemaic Kingdom and the beginning of a new era of Roman dominance in the region. The city of Alexandria, once a beacon of Greek culture and learning, was forever changed by the influx of Roman settlers and the imposition of Roman rule.

As the great Roman historian Suetonius wrote, 'Caesar, having established his power in Alexandria, was hailed as a god by the Egyptians, and his name was included in the list of the gods.' This event was a turning point in the history of the ancient world, setting the stage for the rise of Rome as a global superpower.
